newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH BOSS COUNTERS RAVANELLI REMARKS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH BOSS COUNTERS RAVANELLI REMARKS.

text.p: Middlesbrough manager Bryan Robson hit back on Tuesday at Fabrizio Ravanelli's criticism of training facilities and coaching methods at English clubs.

The seven million pounds ($11.55 million) signing, whose scathing remarks were made in an interview on Italian television, claimed he was forced to train on his own at Middlesbrough using charts supplied by former club Juventus.
Robson denied Ravanelli had been isolated, defended his struggling club's match preparations, and pointed out that Middlesbrough planned to build new training facilities.
"Ravanelli trained on his own when he stayed behind during our pre-season tours but he does not train on his own now," said Robson.
Robson argued that match preparations were different by necessity in England compared to those in Italy.
He pointed out that English teams face a demanding fixture programme where Italian clubs only play at weekends unless they are involved in European competitions.
"The English system takes its toll on players. You cannot overdo it in training otherwise it affects your fitness in matches," said Robson.
